Haysyn Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the oldest of Haysyn's three documented Jewish cemeteries, marked on maps from 1913. Haysyn's Jewish community, present from at least 1765, grew to a majority of the town — over 7,000 people — by 1917, before enduring repeated pogroms and, ultimately, the loss of thousands during the German occupation of 1941–1942, when Jews were also used as forced labor to build a bridge toward Vinnytsia. The town produced three notable Yiddish and English-language literary figures: Avrahm Yarmolinsky, David Bromberg, and Joseph Kerler. This cemetery was demolished around the 1930s, according to a local historian, and multistory residential buildings were eventually constructed on the vacant site in the 1960s.
